goal: Identify the reproducible request-size, output-budget, concurrency, complexity, and gateway conditions that cause CGKN live Provider generation to return 504/520 or become transport-unstable.
acceptance_criteria: Injected interface and quality defects route to affected work only.
Small, medium, and ACFV-scale trials use the same management contracts.
The final report distinguishes planning, implementation, quality, and delivery evidence.

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

quality_metrics.measure: bounded context and affected-work repair at increasing project scale
quality_metrics.target: context remains within configured budgets and unrelated checkpoints remain reusable
quality_metrics.method: generation scale ladder and ACFV-scale trial

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

feedback: Live probes isolate the fault to a monolithic long-output Provider leaf near the upstream 60-second boundary; single samples establish an operational boundary, not an SLA.

worked: Input-size isolation, output-budget ladder, exact-like complex reproduction, and bounded concurrency separated the causal variables.
did_not_work: An 8,000-token complex single-file request crossed the gateway boundary and returned HTTP 520 with no usable content.
experiments: Implement symbol-group leaf planning with a 4,000-5,000-token transport target, deterministic assembly, and section-level resume.
